items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I’d see these guys and I’d ask them questions and this and that, and so they sort of knew me from that... I’d write this bass trombone player, Bill Hughes, the manager, or trumpet player at the time, Sonny Cohn

ctx.x: You mentioned an anecdote about getting to see Count Basie and so forth. Did you have aspirations to play in the big bands that were still around as a young man?

Yeah absolutely. And I started a relationship with some of the guys in the band too because they’d come about three or four times a year to Minnesota, where I was living at the time. And I’d say look what’s your address? And they gave me the address of Willard Alexander, the booking in New York that booked every big band I later found out — you know 660 Madison Avenue, New York, NY 1002 — whatever it was. It was the address, and you could just write, “The guy in the band, Count Basie Orchestra, Willard Alexander,…

O’Clock Jump” I had because I played that with records. You know you stand in a room and you pretend like you’re lead trumpet player and you play with the records, like we’ve all done. And that’s something that everybody has to do at some period in their lives. So yeah I definitely had aspirations to do it, and I’d already done it anyway in drill at home in my basement.
